derivation_notes: Independent sampling gives the effective infectious exposure per contact as q*i. Applying a Holling type-II acquisition probability, (q*i)/(exposure_half_saturation + q*i), to the s*c available susceptible-contact opportunities yields a nonnegative rate that vanishes for s=0 or i=0 and approaches the finite ceiling s*c at high exposure.

scenario_text: Estimate the instantaneous rate at which susceptible people acquire infection under independently sampled contact and infectiousness conditions. The baseline mechanism is infectious contact generation with a contact-limited acquisition response that approaches a finite ceiling at high exposure. Susceptibility and infectious prevalence are treated as externally specified conditions rather than evolving states. The output is an instantaneous epidemiological rate, so no time integration is required.

derivation_notes: The parent saturating acquisition law is retained, but the effective half-saturation is reduced as susceptible availability rises: exposure_half_saturation_eff = exposure_half_saturation/(1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s). This captures the hypothesis that encounter competition within the susceptible pool changes how rapidly additional infectious exposure converts into realized acquisitions while keeping the rate nonnegative, zero at s=0 or i=0, and bounded by s*c at high exposure.
change_summary: Changed the assumption that the acquisition half-saturation is fixed across all susceptible fractions. The successor makes the saturation scale s-dependent, producing different exposure-response curvature across susceptible strata rather than a pure vertical rescaling.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The effective-exposure level at which acquisition reaches half of its contact-limited maximum is fixed and does not vary with the susceptible fraction.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Encounter competition and repeated contact among the shrinking susceptible pool can change how quickly additional infectious exposure converts into new acquisitions, making the apparent saturation scale depend on susceptible availability.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when susceptible_saturation_modulation = 0, so the effective half-saturation becomes the constant exposure_half_saturation.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed s and c, new_infection_rate increases with exposure q*i as a one-parameter Michaelis-Menten saturating curve with a single shared half-saturation scale exposure_half_saturation independent of susceptible availability.
response_change.child_relation: Keep the same bounded contact-limited acquisition mechanism but relax the assumption that the half-saturation scale is fixed: make effective saturation depend on susceptible fraction so that crowding of susceptible encounters changes the curvature of the exposure-response while preserving vanishing at i=0 and s=0 and a finite high-exposure ceiling.
response_change.observable_effect: When q*i is varied at fixed c, the rise toward saturation is steeper or more delayed depending on s; thus two strata with different s show different exposure-response curvature that cannot be matched by one parent half-saturation value.

evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, modest variation in s already reveals that the exposure-response bends differently at the same q*i; in holdout, broader s variation extends this same curvature difference rather than introducing a new mechanism.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where susceptible dependence of the effective half-saturation vanishes, so the saturation scale becomes the constant exposure_half_saturation for all s.

evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Encounter competition and repeated contact among the shrinking susceptible pool can change how quickly additional infectious exposure converts into new acquisitions, making the apparent saturation scale depend on susceptible availability.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it introduces a distinct susceptibility-controlled relaxation scale inside the nonlinear denominator, changing the shape of the exposure-response family across s rather than merely shifting one global gain or one global threshold.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The effective-exposure level at which acquisition reaches half of its contact-limited maximum is fixed and does not vary with the susceptible fraction.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The effective half-saturation scale is modulated by susceptible availability, so different susceptible fractions have different exposure-response curvature even under the same contact rate and infectious exposure.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Set susceptible_saturation_modulation = 0 to recover the parent expression exactly.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: For fixed c, compare normalized rate new_infection_rate/(s*c) versus q*i across two admissible susceptible fractions with 0 < s <= 1. The parent predicts the same Michaelis-Menten curve in both strata, while the child predicts different curvature because the effective saturation scale is exposure_half_saturation/(1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s).
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent cannot reproduce this pattern because its normalized mapping new_infection_rate/(s*c) depends only on q*i through one common exposure_half_saturation, so all s strata share the same curve shape. The child creates an s-dependent denominator scale, yielding a family of distinct curvature profiles across s that no single parent parameter set can match simultaneously over conditions where both s and q*i vary.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes a single susceptibility-independent exposure half-saturation, so all susceptible strata share the same normalized exposure-response shape after multiplication by s.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The effective-exposure level at which acquisition reaches half of its contact-limited maximum is fixed and does not vary with the susceptible fraction.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Encounter competition and repeated contact among the shrinking susceptible pool can change how quickly additional infectious exposure converts into new acquisitions, making the apparent saturation scale depend on susceptible availability.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the fixed-threshold assumption already present in the saturating acquisition term, not to add a wholly separate process. The parent mapping is s*c times a saturating function of q*i with one shared half-saturation parameter, so changing s only rescales the curve vertically. Scientifically, if the susceptible pool is sparse or dense, the same infectious exposure can be distributed differently across susceptible encounter opportunities, altering how quickly the acquisition response approaches its contact-limited ceiling. Vary q*i while holding c fixed and compare two admissible susceptible fractions s1 and s2 within 0<s<=1. In the parent, the ratio new_infection_rate/(s*c) as a function of q*i is identical for both strata, because curvature is controlled only by exposure_half_saturation. In the child, that normalized curve changes with s, giving an observable curvature contrast at intermediate exposures. This is a true target-mapping change, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because the predicted instantaneous rate for the same supplied inputs changes. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce different normalized q*i-response shapes across varying s; it can only choose one common threshold and one common curvature family. The refinement remains scientifically admissible because the rate stays nonnegative, vanishes when s=0 or i=0, and can be constructed to retain a finite high-exposure bound.

derivation_notes: The parent assumes susceptible fraction only shifts the exposure half-saturation scale. Here the remaining susceptible pool is allowed to alter how concentrated or cooperative infectious opportunities are, so the effective exposure term enters with an s-dependent exponent, changing curvature while preserving the same contact-limited ceiling s*c.
change_summary: Relaxed the fixed-shape Michaelis assumption by letting susceptible fraction control the exposure-response curvature as well as the threshold scale. This creates an s-dependent competition between the baseline half-saturation term and the transformed exposure term, making saturation more abrupt at high s.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Susceptible fraction alters only the effective half-saturation scale, while the exposure-response shape is fixed.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Heterogeneity among remaining susceptible individuals can concentrate acquisition into more exposure-sensitive subgroups as susceptibility availability changes, modifying the curvature of the exposure-acquisition relation.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when susceptible_curvature_modulation = 0, so the exposure exponent becomes 1.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent uses one susceptible-modulated half-saturation scale, so at fixed s the dependence of new_infection_rate on exposure q*i is a standard single Michaelis-type rise with a fixed shape, and changing s mainly rescales the overall prefactor and shifts that one threshold.
response_change.child_relation: Refine the acquisition response so that susceptible availability also changes the curvature of the exposure-response, not only its half-saturation location, making the q*i to new_infection_rate mapping steeper at low exposure and more abruptly saturating when s is high.
response_change.observable_effect: Across low versus high susceptible fraction, with c fixed and exposure q*i swept through the half-saturation regime, the child shows different normalized response shapes after matching low-exposure slope or half-saturation, whereas the parent can only shift one common saturating curve.

assumption_audit.mechanism: Infectious prevalence can alter overlap, independence, or redundancy among infectious contacts, so the effective exposure threshold for acquisition can depend on i in addition to s even when total q*i is matched.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when infectious_threshold_modulation = 0.

The parent already includes susceptible-dependent curvature and saturation, but it still imposes a single threshold in the exposure coordinate q*i for each s. Scientifically, independently sampled contact and infectiousness conditions need not make prevalence composition irrelevant: with fixed susceptible fraction s and fixed per-contact opportunity q, changing i can alter whether exposure is spread across many infectious contacts or concentrated into fewer opportunities, which changes redundancy and therefore the apparent threshold for acquisition. The concrete distinguishing condition is: hold s and q fixed, compare two admissible i levels in a moderate regime where q*i is large enough to generate measurable infection but not so large that the response is fully saturated. The parent predicts that the response depends only on q*i, so data collapsed by q*i must coincide under one shared parameter set. The child predicts a shifted threshold across i levels even after matching or comparing nearby q*i values. This is a changed target mapping, not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation, because new_infection_rate itself changes as a function of supplied inputs. No new degree of freedom is needed conceptually because the refinement can be implemented by making the existing threshold structure depend on i using additional fixed parameters in the successor equation. Limitation: if all observed conditions remain extremely close to i=0 or deep in saturation, the contrast will be weak.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make one process depend jointly on two declared quantities.

scenario_text: Estimate the instantaneous rate at which susceptible people acquire infection under independently sampled contact and infectiousness conditions. The baseline mechanism is infectious contact generation with a contact-limited acquisition response that approaches a finite ceiling at high exposure. Susceptibility and infectious prevalence are treated as externally specified conditions rather than evolving states. The output is an instantaneous epidemiological rate, so no time integration is required.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed s, the acquisition response is a Hill-like saturating function of effective exposure q*i with a single half-saturation scale exposure_half_saturation/(1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s).
response_change.child_relation: Replace the single exposure half-saturation scale with an exposure threshold that also depends on infectious prevalence i, so the q*i level needed for a given fraction of the contact-limited maximum shifts with i as well as s.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding s and q fixed, low-i and high-i conditions show different horizontal placement of the exposure-response curve; the child allows earlier or later saturation as infectious prevalence changes, whereas the parent can only change the curve through q*i and cannot move the threshold independently of exposure magnitude.

derivation_notes: The parent Hill-like acquisition law is retained but the exposure-response exponent is re-derived to depend on infectious prevalence as well as susceptible fraction, representing prevalence-dependent redundancy or heterogeneity in infectious contacts. This preserves nonnegativity and the contact-limited ceiling s*c while allowing i to alter transition sharpness in addition to threshold location.
change_summary: Relaxed the assumption that infectious prevalence only shifts the effective threshold by adding an infectious-prevalence contribution to the saturation exponent. The successor therefore changes the shape of the q*i to infection-rate curve with i at fixed s, not just its horizontal position.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: All i-dependence beyond the multiplicative exposure term q*i acts only through the effective half-saturation scale, while the curvature exponent depends only on s.
assumption_audit.mechanism: As infectious prevalence rises, infectious contacts can become more redundant or more independently distributed across susceptibles, changing the cooperativity of exposure conversion into acquisition even at the same aggregate exposure q*i.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting infectious_curvature_modulation = 0 recovers the parent law exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed s, the rate is a single Hill-like saturating function of exposure q*i with one shared curvature exponent 1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s and one effective half-saturation scale modified by s and i.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same bounded contact-limited structure but relax the assumption that infectious prevalence only shifts the threshold; allow infectious prevalence to also alter the steepness/cooperativity of the exposure-acquisition response, so the q*i to rate curve changes shape with i as well as location.
response_change.observable_effect: For two admissible infectious prevalences with the same susceptible fraction held fixed, the low-exposure rise and mid-exposure sharpness can differ even after matching the half-saturation location; the parent can slide the curve horizontally with i but cannot reproduce an i-dependent steepness change with one shared parameter set.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Visible when q*i traverses the transition region around the effective half-saturation and i varies over a non-negligible admissible range while s is held fixed away from zero; weak at very low exposure, near-complete saturation, or i so small that prevalence-dependent steepness changes are negligible.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate variation in i already reveals that equalized threshold location does not align the full response curves; in holdout, extending to higher i amplifies the same mechanism through stronger prevalence-dependent steepness differences without changing the bounded high-exposure ceiling.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Setting the added infectious-prevalence curvature effect to zero recovers the parent law exactly.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: As infectious people become more prevalent, contacts may become more redundant or more independently distributed across susceptible individuals, changing how sharply additional exposure converts into acquisition even at the same aggregate q*i.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the exponent governing the saturating transition is now input-dependent in i, changing the family of admissible curve shapes rather than merely rescaling or shifting one shared shape.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Infectious prevalence affects the target mapping only through q*i and the threshold factor (1 + infectious_threshold_modulation*i), leaving the Hill-like curvature fixed at a given s.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Infectious prevalence also modulates the curvature exponent of the bounded acquisition response, so i changes transition sharpness as well as threshold.
evolution_contract.after_fragment: s*c*(q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i)/(exposure_half_saturation/((1 + susceptible_saturation_modulation*s)*(1 + infectious_threshold_modulation*i)) + (q*i)**(1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s + infectious_curvature_modulation*i))
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Hold s fixed at an intermediate positive value and vary q so that q*i spans the transition region for two different admissible i values. In the parent, after accounting for the i-dependent threshold shift, both curves share the same steepness because the exponent is fixed at 1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s. In the child, the same comparison shows different low-exposure rise and mid-transition sharpness because the exponent also changes with i. This is directly observable in the scored mapping from supplied inputs (s,i,q,c) to new_infection_rate and is strongest away from near-zero exposure and away from full saturation.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent cannot generally match two i-conditioned response curves with different steepness at the same fixed s because it has only one curvature value 1 + susceptible_curvature_modulation*s for that s. Retuning exposure_half_saturation or infectious_threshold_modulation only shifts the curve location with i; it does not create prevalence-dependent sharpening or broadening once threshold location is matched.

derivation_notes: The parent assumes all exposure-acquisition behavior follows one single Hill-type phase. Here that is relaxed by allowing infectious prevalence to alter the saturation shape through a bounded redundancy factor, representing the shift from more independent rare opportunities at low prevalence toward overlapping repeated opportunities at higher prevalence.
change_summary: Added a prevalence-dependent saturation-shape refinement that activates with i and is tempered by total exposure q*i. This changes the input-to-rate mapping directly, allowing different low-i and higher-i approach-to-ceiling behavior than a single Hill family can supply.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: All infectious-contact opportunities are effectively summarized by one homogeneous saturating exposure-response phase, with no additional prevalence-dependent transition between near-independent and redundant contact opportunity sampling.
assumption_audit.mechanism: As infectious prevalence rises, contacts experienced by susceptibles can shift from approximately independent rare opportunities to more redundant repeated opportunities from overlapping infectious sources, changing the shape of saturation itself rather than only the threshold or Hill exponent.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent when infectious_redundancy_shape = 0.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed s, the acquisition probability per susceptible is a single Hill-type saturating function of aggregate exposure q*i, with one shared effective threshold and one shared curvature value determined only by linear modulation in s and i.
response_change.child_relation: At fixed s, the exposure-acquisition relation transitions from near-linear response at low infectious prevalence to stronger saturation at higher infectious prevalence because infectious prevalence not only shifts threshold/curvature but also changes how close contact opportunities are to independent across susceptibles, producing a prevalence-dependent saturation shape that cannot be represented by one single-phase Hill form over all i.
response_change.observable_effect: When q and s are held fixed and i is varied from low to moderate values, the child can show a delayed onset of strong saturation at low i but a sharper approach to the contact ceiling at higher i; the parent can only bend this tradeoff through one Hill family and cannot match both low-i near-proportional growth and high-i compressed approach-to-ceiling with one shared parameter set.
